content:
Spotify paid subscribers have surpassed the 300 million mark, setting an important milestone for the audio streaming service in its competition with Apple Music.

Spotify celebrates paid subscribers crossing 300 million

The company revealed the figure in its second-quarter earnings report, with Premium subscribers reaching 300 million, up 9% year-on-year, and monthly active users at 777 million.

Spotify has gradually expanded its paid service from pure music streaming to areas including audiobooks and podcasts.

Since Apple announced Apple Music had surpassed 60 million subscribers in 2019, it has not disclosed related figures. However, the company recently announced a larger (but fundamentally different) milestone: 1.5 billion paid subscriptions across its services.

This total covers multiple Apple services, including Apple Music, iCloud+, and Apple TV. A large portion is believed to come from third-party app subscriptions sold through the App Store, from which Apple takes a 15% to 30% cut of transactions.

Both Spotify and Apple Music raised prices this year. Spotify raised the US individual monthly fee from US$11.99 to US$12.99 in January, while Apple Music raised its individual monthly fee from US$10.99 to US$11.99 last month.

Apple Music and Spotify compete for users

Spotify's growth continues a string of new features and updates this year, including:

  • Taste Profile controls
  • SongDNA
  • Distraction-free mode
  • Redesigned iPad app
  • Video podcast upgrades
  • AI remix tools
  • Background download feature
  • Expanded playlist pinning feature
  • Snapchat integration

As for Apple Music, it will launch more new features next month with iOS 27, including redesigned artist and album pages, improved AutoMix transitions, faster playback speed, a landscape playback interface, and "Siri AI integration".
